codex.worst_flaw: The pilot bundles private feedback, crew reporting, and recognition, so even with comparison crews it cannot determine whether reporting or recognition adds value beyond private feedback alone.

claude.worst_flaw: The design has no event or policy versioning, no independent shadow validation before launch, and no named appeal owner or turnaround time. Its learning plan also lacks a power or sample-size estimate, and its comparison crews are optional, so a 10-point lift could just be novelty or seasonal drift.

holistic.reason: It is careful on union trust, privacy, verification and a clean baseline-and-comparison design, but the only incentive is a crew thank-you with no tangible reward, the credit and fallback rules are heavy, and a 90-minute weekly audit budget for 300 staff is thin, so awareness, motivation and lasting habit change look modest.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot needs a stronger safety audit before launch because a technician can earn credit for a complete digital form even when the audit misses skipped physical checks or unreported hazards.

claude.worst_flaw: The 15-point scale and 10-point retention thresholds have no stated sample size or uncertainty handling, and the fallback to a before/after baseline when no comparison crews exist cannot separate the programme's effect from app fixes, seasonal case mix or the novelty of a new app; event and policy versioning plus shadow validation before scoring are only partly specified.

holistic.reason: Unusually careful on safety, union consultation, denominator integrity and a pause rule, but it relies on private non-material milestones that may feel weak, and it removes all incentives at the end, so a lasting effect depends on whether the workflow fixes remove real friction.

claude.worst_flaw: Quality checking relies on a 10-job weekly sample with no check on whether the hazard answers are true (for example, an inspector observing on site or comparing answers against incident or near-miss data), so a fast tick-box checklist would earn credit and pass the audit unless it was obviously missing.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot is not launchable as specified because a timely checklist can earn credit even when safety steps were skipped or hazards went unreported, and the audit has no independent check for either failure.

holistic.reason: Safety-first, union-co-designed, non-punitive and with strong diagnosis and audit controls, but it relies on private feedback with no rewards, so it is likely to be low-salience and to produce modest lasting change unless app friction is actually fixed.

claude.worst_flaw: The design only compares the pilot with the team's own earlier baseline, so it cannot tell how much the goal messages added beyond the routing fixes and review slots. Its own text admits this, and it still uses the result to decide whether to keep the approach.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot introduces submission confirmation and weekly goals together, so its historical comparison cannot show whether the goals add value over plain feedback.

holistic.reason: It is carefully designed, private, and non-competitive, and it fixes routing and protected time first, which suits sceptical engineers. But the credit rules are intricate, the weekly admin load is nontrivial, and the end-of-pilot design means the behaviour may fade unless the kept routing and review slots do the real work.

codex.worst_flaw: Without a comparison period or group using routing and private feedback alone, the pilot cannot tell whether shared progress updates improve review response times.

claude.worst_flaw: The learning design is a single-team before/after comparison with no concurrent comparison or plain-support arm, so it cannot separate the programme's effect from the routing and backup fixes or from seasonal workload, and the design admits the result is only feasibility evidence.

holistic.reason: Unusually careful, diagnosis-first design with quality checks, private feedback and a no-badges stance suits sceptical engineers, but the single invitation in the review request is a low-salience nudge, and retiring the weekly updates plus a fixed 80% threshold leaves lasting change to routing fixes alone.

claude.worst_flaw: The learning design has no comparison condition and only a pre-holiday baseline, so it cannot separate the reminder and feedback effect from seasonal workload or plain routing fixes. Leave and absence are also not separated from late reviews, which puts unavailable reviewers in the late count.

codex.worst_flaw: The expansion decision relies on a historical baseline that cannot isolate the effect of reminders and shared progress from routing fixes or changes in PR mix.

holistic.reason: Unusually careful, anti-gaming and sceptic-friendly design with diagnosis, quality sampling and private feedback, but the incentive is mostly nudges and routing fixes with no real reward, so awareness and post-pilot persistence are modest and the admin overhead is real.

codex.worst_flaw: The scale decision relies on a before-and-after comparison that cannot isolate the effect of ward recognition from private feedback, workflow fixes, or changes in the opportunities observers sample.

claude.worst_flaw: The design has no comparison group and no test of plain feedback against the added recognition. It also leaves the ward 'pilot targets' and minimum audit counts undefined. A before/after rise in logging, measured on sparse monthly observer samples that observer presence can inflate, cannot show the incremental value it uses to decide whether to scale.

holistic.reason: It is careful on safety, privacy and measurement, but the logging burden falls on busy nurses with only private feedback and one huddle thank-you as motivation, and ending prompts on April 30 leaves little to sustain the habit.

codex.worst_flaw: Launch should wait until the hospital validates that observers can reliably match hygiene actions to kiosk entries without collecting identifiers or disrupting care.

claude.worst_flaw: The core measure is unreliable: verified logging is only measured while an observer is present, which invites the Hawthorne effect, and observers must match entries without collecting identifiers. There is also no comparison ward, no minimum sample size and no replayable event history, so a before/after gain cannot be credited to the programme.

holistic.reason: Careful, safety-minded and measurable design with good pause rules and privacy guardrails, but the dual-observer verification is heavy, there is no tangible incentive or salience beyond private confirmations and ward feedback, and the effect is likely to fade once prompts end.

claude.worst_flaw: The target is one kiosk entry per shift, and nothing checks entries against real hand-hygiene events, so 'uptake' can rise with no link to clinical value. The uncontrolled before/after design across three wards also cannot isolate the effect from seasonal or ward-level change.

codex.worst_flaw: A ward can meet the expansion threshold through inaccurate kiosk entries because the observer audits measure clinical compliance without verifying that credited entries correspond to real hand-hygiene events.

holistic.reason: Well-guarded design (skip-when-busy, one credit per shift, no individual performance use, care-delay pause, separate audit metric) that I'd approve as a pilot, but a private progress message and a shift-huddle prompt are weak motivators for busy nurses, and with prompts and goals removed on April 30 the habit would likely fade within three months.

codex.worst_flaw: The scale rule relies on a before-and-after comparison that cannot show whether weekly goals and team progress add value beyond the workflow fixes and private confirmation.

claude.worst_flaw: The design has no comparison group and treats the before-and-after coverage change as only feasibility evidence, yet it uses that comparison to decide whether to scale. It also leaves a gap between its own goals and its scale rule. The weekly goal of 3 credits is not tied to the 30% coverage target. Resolution time, a likely displacement effect with the CSAT bonus at stake, is never measured; only CSAT is checked.

holistic.reason: Rigorous measurement, diagnosis, and guardrails protect CSAT, but the incentive is only private goals and progress copy with no real reward, the pilot ends abruptly, and its own risks admit documentation costs more time than reuse saves.

codex.worst_flaw: The scale decision relies on a before-and-after comparison that cannot distinguish the effect of weekly goals and progress feedback from workflow fixes or changes in ticket mix.

claude.worst_flaw: The design judges success with an uncontrolled before-and-after comparison and no comparison group or plain-support arm, so it can't separate the programme's effect from workflow fixes, seasonality or case mix, and the 15/10-point thresholds have no sample-size or uncertainty reasoning.

holistic.reason: Rigorous, auditable and well-guarded against gaming, but the motivation is only private progress messages with no rewards or recognition, and the credit rules are complex for a busy agent to notice or care about, so lasting change after March 7 depends on the workflow fixes.

codex.worst_flaw: The baseline-only pilot cannot tell whether weekly goals and shared progress improve adoption beyond workflow fixes and immediate feedback.

claude.worst_flaw: The design relies on a before/after baseline with no concurrent comparison arm. It also never tests whether the 'half of eligible volume capped at five' goal adds anything over plain confirmation feedback, so the effect of the incentive design itself cannot be isolated.

holistic.reason: Rigorous design with diagnosis-first, QA sampling, privacy guardrails and honest stop rules, but KB credit carries zero pay weight and relies on private nudges, so motivation is modest and the extra closeout work may fade once prompts end.
